attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, not a quotation of someone else.

semantics.note: Firm 'will' keeps the copyright-rewrite antecedent and the 'in the end' horizon. The vivid wording ('nobody', 'eating its own tail') may be partly rhetorical, and the contract flags this.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary. It properly requires an enacted change for the antecedent and notes there is no deadline or quality measure. The result turns on how the jurisdiction, the scale of change, and 'good content' are read.

evidence.note: UK government report dated 2026-03-18 drops the opt-out exception and proposes gathering more evidence. It records a policy process, not an enacted change, so the antecedent is not established.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. The packet does not show that the antecedent (an enacted copyright rewrite favouring GenAI) occurred, and the UK report shows reform stalled. No conclusive event settles the eventual outcome, so it cannot be scored by the cutoff.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his own post about what he and Southen showed.

semantics.note: 'Same kind of regurgitation' refers to the NYT text-model regurgitation in context, so the normalisation is faithful. 'Prone' gives no frequency threshold.

contract.note: Reading it as demonstrated susceptibility to reproducing identifiable source images, not equal rates and not legal infringement, is fair and ordinary. It also excludes the speaker's own demonstrations, as the rules require.

evidence.note: Independent Carlini et al. preprint (Jan 2023, before the post) shows diffusion models memorize training images and emit them.
Independent Somepalli et al. preprint (Dec 2022) finds Stable Diffusion blatantly copying training data.
Webster (May 2023) notes extraction is hard and works for few samples. This limits claims about frequency but does not negate susceptibility.

reviews.rationale: Two independent studies published before the post show image generators reproducing identifiable training images, which is the same kind of failure as text regurgitation. e3 shows this is rare, but 'prone' as read in the contract needs only demonstrated susceptibility.
